Subject: Hosted API commit uplift — onramp plan & tier laddering confirmation

Evan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, BrightPaths is looking to increase its hosted commit from the current 3M tokens/mo to a stepped 6M then 9M commit over the first 90 days of the next term. I put together a suggested onramp structure we can operationalize:

- Month 1: 6M committed tokens, access to a 20% burst pocket (pay-as-used beyond the commit at burst rate).
- Month 2: 7.5M committed (auto-step if Month 1 utilization >= 90% of commit).
- Month 3 onward: 9M committed (final tier) with soft-throttle thresholds to protect latency SLOs.

Pricing and ratebanding we discussed: two-tier unit pricing (base commit unit, burst unit). Our proposal includes a 10% discount on the base commit compared to current list pricing, and a reduced burst rate for the first 90 days to smooth migration risk.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll share an SOW + revised quote for your procurement.
2) Karthik will confirm final rate numbers and any SLA language we need to add.
3) We lock the DocuSign packet once procurement confirms the schedule.

Attaching a high-level usage export for October so you can see the burst profile. Happy to jump on a short call with Allison and your procurement team.

Best,
Hannah

Hannah / Marissa —

Thanks for the context. Quick numbers below (ballpark, legal/commercial can refine):

Proposal (unit = per-1k-token equivalent):
- Base commit unit (post 10% commit discount): $0.65 per 1k tokens at 6M commit
- Month 2 step pricing (7.5M): $0.62 per 1k tokens (when auto-step triggers)
- Final 9M tier: $0.58 per 1k tokens
- Standard burst rate: $1.30 per 1k tokens
- Introductory 90-day burst rate: $0.85 per 1k tokens (to reduce migration risk)

Other commercial terms:
- 60-day notice window: we can gate auto-step so the customer receives a notification 60 days before an automatic step would take effect. We will not auto-increase without explicit acceptance after that notice — that satisfies their billing cycle ask.
- Capped burst spend: we can offer a $50k capped-burst protection for the first 90 days implemented as a soft cap with invoice-level credit if exceeded. Hard caps are risky for latency-sensitive apps. Recommend the invoice credit approach and a monthly alert if usage approaches 80% of the capped threshold.

Ops/SLA impact: enabling the burst pocket + soft cap has no SLA penalty; however, guaranteeing an uncapped burst at low rates indefinitely would. We'll include a clause that allows fallback to soft-throttle if burst spending exceeds the protection window without manual approval.

I'll draft the commercial summary and a short SOW checklist (billing lines, start date, onramp schedule) and circulate by EOD Monday.

—Karthik
